html:
The leader of Togo's independence movement and its first president, from independence on 27 April 1960 until he was shot dead in a coup on 13 January 1963.

From a family of Afro-Brazilian merchants, he studied at the London School of Economics and managed a large trading firm in Lome. His Committee of Togolese Unity, strong among the Ewe, won the 1958 election held under UN watch. As president he kept his distance from France and cut spending, refusing to take on soldiers returning from the French army. Some of them killed him at the gate of the US embassy. Gnassingbe Eyadema later said he fired the shot. It was the first coup in post-colonial French-speaking Africa and set a pattern that spread across the region.
sum: The leader of Togo's independence movement and its first president, from independence on 27 April 1960 until he was shot dead in a coup on 13 January 1963.
